1.0.0.en: 1 The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake. 2 And he said, “The LORD will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the habitations of the shepherds shall mourn, and the top of Carmel shall wither.”

1.0.1.en: “The words of Amos, who was among the herdmen of Tekoa, which he saw concerning Israel, in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel, two years before the earthquake” [1].

1.0.2.en: The prophet Amos was not ashamed to highlight his work as a shepherd of sheep in Tekoa, that is, that he came from the poor classes, especially as he was a gatherer of sycamore fruit, which none does but one in great need. As for the absence of his father’s name, it is because he was from a poor and unknown family.

1.0.3.en: It is remarkable that he says: “The words of Amos… which he saw,” and not which he heard or delivered, affirming that the words he proclaims here are not from himself but are the fruit of divine visions and revelations by the Holy Spirit.

1.0.4.en: He has specified the place of his upbringing and the date of his prophetic work, two matters which we discussed earlier in the introduction.

1.1.0.en: He said: “The LORD will roar from Zion, and utter his voice from Jerusalem; and the habitations of the shepherds shall mourn, and the top of Carmel shall wither” [2].

1.1.1.en: This is the opening of his prophecy, and perhaps Amos’s dwelling in Tekoa on the edge of the wilderness gave him the experience of the roaring of the lion in the wilderness, which terrifies the shepherds and strikes dread into the life of the farmers. The prophet Amos likened God in His wrath against sin to the lion that roars, saying: “The lion hath roared, who will not fear? the Lord GOD hath spoken, who can but prophesy?” (Amos 3:8). The roaring of the lion does not arise from emptiness, nor is it uttered without cause: “Will a lion roar in the forest, when he hath no prey?” (Amos 3:4).

1.1.2.en: The prophets Hosea and Joel spoke of God, blessed be His name, as a lion who utters his voice so that heaven and earth tremble, and all realize that He is the refuge of His people and a stronghold for them, dwelling in their midst in His holy mountain in Jerusalem, His sanctuary, so that no stranger comes near them (Joel 3:16-17). He roars and gathers His people from Egypt and Assyria and settles them in their houses (Hos 11:10-11). Here, however, the prophet Amos sees the holy God as a lion couching in Zion, uttering his voice roaring because of the sins of Israel and Judah and all the surrounding nations. He cannot bear sin to approach His sanctuary and surround Him, so He roars and shakes the foundations of sin and shatters the works of the old man; fire goes out of His mouth and burns its palaces and scatters its being!

1.1.3.en: When the lion utters his voice, the habitations of the shepherds mourn, and the top of Carmel, the most fertile region, withers, for all realize that the voice of the LORD dries up whatever has arisen upon evil, and shatters every fruit of corruption!

1.1.4.en: The word of the LORD is not spoken for flattery or hypocrisy or wavering between good and evil, but for shattering evil in order to establish good, or crucifying the old man to announce the rising of the new man. The Lion who came out of the tribe of Judah roared, affirming this: “No man putteth a piece of new cloth unto an old garment, for that which is put in to fill it up taketh from the garment, and the rent is made worse. Neither do men put new wine into old bottles: else the bottles break, and the wine runneth out, and the bottles perish: but they put new wine into new bottles, and both are preserved” (Mt 9:16-17). As St. Ambrose says: [For this reason the Lord forbids us to mix the new with the old, and the Apostle forbids putting on the new garment over the old; rather we put off the old and put on the new, so that we may not be found naked (2 Cor 5:2-4)].

1.1.5.en: Jacob realized this when he blessed his son Judah, from whose loins would come forth the Lion who roars against sin and terrifies death, saying: “Judah is a lion’s whelp: from the prey, my son, thou art gone up: he stooped down, he couched as a lion, and as a lioness; who shall rouse him up?” (Gen 49:9). He saw Him couching as a lion on the Cross, roaring against the sin that corrupted human life in order to kill his prey, the devil and his works, granting humanity sanctification and making it Zion and the holy Jerusalem!

1.1.6.en: In truth, the prophecy of Amos as a whole is the roaring of the Lion from Zion. It began with terrifying chastisements, the fire that burns the palaces and shatters the fortresses and scatters the inhabitants, whether of the nations or of the Jews, not that they might remain a ruin without inhabitant, but that at the end of the prophecy He might open wide the doors of hope; instead of palaces He raises up the tabernacle of David that is fallen, and instead of fortresses He Himself repairs their breaches and raises up their ruins, and builds them as in the days of old and dwells Himself in their midst, so that His name is called upon all the nations (Amos 9:11-12). He pulls down and builds, plucks up and plants, shatters the old man to raise up the new in us! This is the roaring of the Lion from Zion, who utters His voice from Jerusalem, His sanctuary!

1.2.0.en: 3 Thus saith the LORD; “For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have threshed Gilead with threshing instruments of iron: 4 But I will send a fire into the house of Hazael, which shall devour the palaces of Benhadad. 5 I will break also the bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant from the plain of Aven, and him that holdeth the sceptre from the house of Eden: and the people of Syria shall go into captivity unto Kir, saith the LORD.”

1.2.1.en: In His chastisements of the nations and Judah He took one course in announcing the One who presents the chastisement, that is, “God Himself,” and their three and four transgressions, and the not turning back from the chastisement, and the sending of a consuming fire… All these shared together in speaking of the chastisement of all the nations and Judah, but each nation was marked by a particular sin or sins of its own.

1.2.2.en: At the beginning of every chastisement He says: “Thus saith the LORD…” (vv. 3, 6, 9, 11, 13; ch. 2:1, 4, 6). Although not all the nations worship Him, He is the Judge of all, the God of the whole earth, who judges all and cares also for all!

1.2.3.en: As for His speaking of their three and four transgressions, these two numbers point here to many meanings, of which we mention:

1.2.4.en: First: the number 3 points to the human soul as being in the image and likeness of the Holy Trinity, and the number 4 points to the body as being taken from the earth with its four directions (east, west, north, south); so it is as though God chastises us for our sins of the soul (such as pride and malice) and the sins of the body (such as love of luxury, gluttony and bodily lusts). As St. Augustine says: [For sins are committed either by the mind, as by the will alone, or by the works of the body also, and then they are visible… For three is the nature of the soul, and four because of the body, since man is composed of both].

1.2.5.en: Second: St. Jerome sees that the three and four transgressions mean sin that has developed to its third generation and its fourth generation, turning from a mere thought in the mind to its declaration through word, then deed, and finally becoming a habit. God in His long-suffering does not punish a man when sin stirs in his mind, but as it is said: “visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children unto the third and fourth generation” (Num 14:18). This means that God does not punish us immediately for our thoughts, but for the evil deeds and the habits of sin that spring from them, as was said by the mouth of Amos: “For three transgressions of the city, such and such, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof.”

1.2.6.en: Again St. Jerome comments on these three and four transgressions that they are:

1.2.9.en: c. Not repenting of it or continuing in it (the third transgression).

1.2.11.en: Among his words: [Now what (the prophet) says is this: You accepted evil and I forgave you; you committed sin and I pardoned you; you did not repent of it and I gave you an excuse; will you also teach sin?! This is what Scripture meant concerning the three and four transgressions].

1.2.12.en: These are the three and four transgressions from which He does not turn back, but sends a fire that burns the palaces of their evil, the fire of His wrath against sin. He cannot bear sin, but He loves sinners! Perhaps this fire is also the natural fruit of sin, the consuming fire, so God leaves man to reap the fruit of his work, to embrace the fire of his sin, which burns his vain palaces that carry glittering, temporary sights.

1.2.13.en: This concerns the nations in general; now we speak of each nation separately.

1.2.14.en: Damascus is the capital of Syria (Aram), and Israel lived for nearly a century in a state of terror of Aram, and some contemporaries of Amos witnessed the war that Hazael king of Aram and his son Benhadad stirred up against Israel (2 Kgs 8:7-15, 28-29; 10:32-33; 13:3-7, 22-25). Gilead, east of the Jordan and north of Syria, was the theatre of this bitter war, which was marked by cruelty and brutality, so that we see Elisha weeping, and when Hazael asks him, before seizing the kingdom, the secret of his weeping, he answers: “Because I know the evil that thou wilt do unto the children of Israel: their strong holds wilt thou set on fire, and their young men wilt thou slay with the sword, and wilt dash their children, and rip up their women with child” (2 Kgs 8:12).

1.2.15.en: The fruit of this cruelty is:

1.3.0.en: First: the fire burns the palace of King Hazael, the stirrer of wars, and his son Benhadad [4]. If this king and his son thought themselves able to shatter the kingdom of God and occupy it, God with the fire of His justice returns their work upon them, so the fire of their evil turns back upon their palace, the center of their authority, the place of their planning, and the place of their security and safety… and it burns and is destroyed.

1.3.1.en: In bitterness I say that our inner Hazael is the “human Ego,” which occupies the heart as its palace, and it and the evils it begets (Benhadad) set about using man with all his energies, potentials, gifts and abilities to work on behalf of evil, instead of the Lord reigning in the heart so that man may work as instruments of righteousness for God. In truth, while the “I” thinks that it is able to reign and rule and dwell securely in its inner palace, it brings upon itself a fire that burns its potentials and loses all its authority.

1.3.2.en: Then let us leave our inner palace to our Lord Jesus instead of Hazael and Benhadad, to be His dwelling and the center of His kingdom, our Lord declaring His Kingdom in it with power, so that the fires of sin, especially the “I,” cannot approach it because it is aflame with heavenly fire, with the Holy Spirit Himself, who shapes it from day to day that it may reach the measure of the fullness of Christ, and takes it from glory to glory, to enter with it in Christ Jesus into the bosom of the Father, and it will rest there forever!

1.3.3.en: Let us surrender our palace to the heavenly King with His fiery Spirit, so that Hazael no longer dwells in us with his son Benhadad.

1.3.4.en: Second: He broke the impregnable fortresses that surround Damascus, not that man may live without fortresses, but that instead of fortresses of stone the Lord Himself may be found as his stronghold and the refuge of his life. For when human arms of stone are present, man leans on them; therefore the Lord shatters them to give us the eternal arms instead, and says: “I will love thee, O LORD, my strength. The LORD is my rock, and my fortress, and my deliverer; my God, my rock, in whom I will take refuge; my buckler, and the horn of my salvation, and my refuge” (Ps 18:1-2).

1.3.5.en: Let the transient walls of stone of Damascus be pulled down, that God may offer us Himself, the Rock of Ages, a wall of rock that the serpent cannot approach, nor can it deceive us while we are in Him; we enter Him and rest, and He is a blazing divine wall of fire that surrounds us and kindles our depths, so that we may be like the heavenly beings, “his ministers a flaming fire” (Ps 104:4).

1.3.6.en: Third: the plain of Aven is turned into a ruin without inhabitant, and it is also called the valley of vanity, or the valley of idols… For when evil works in a man, he thinks he has acquired human wisdom able to enrich him, and he gains much at the expense of others, and behold, he sets up in his heart a valley of vanity or a center of idol worship. He buys emptiness with evil, and acquires deprivation through malice and cunning! This is the lot of the wicked, of whom the psalmist said: “For they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither as the green herb” (Ps 37:2).

1.3.7.en: Fourth: every great man “that holdeth the sceptre” dies in the house of Eden, or in the house of delight and luxury, so that man loses in it everything great and everything strong through his absorption in temporal pleasures and luxuries.

1.3.8.en: Fifth: the captivity of the Arameans to Kir, the kingdom of the Medes, which was fulfilled historically as is recorded in (2 Kgs 16:9; Isa 22:5-6).

1.3.9.en: Who are these Arameans, the inhabitants of Jerusalem, over whom Hazael and his son Benhadad reign, but the energies of man and his abilities and his psychological, mental (intellectual) and bodily gifts?! For when Hazael, that is, the “I,” reigns over them, they turn into slavery and work on behalf of the kingdom of the Medes. Man loses his energies, not that he lives without them, but he lives with energies that have been directed to evil and have deviated from their exalted mission. Man with all his potentials turns to work on behalf of the enemy of good under the slavery of the devil, instead of lifting them up by the Holy Spirit on behalf of the kingdom of God!

1.3.10.en: In short, the fruit of what Hazael and his son Benhadad did, that is, the fruit of pride and self-reliance, is that man loses his inner palace, and his fortresses to which he fled are pulled down, and he loses all greatness and strength as in the house of Aven, and acquires deprivation in the house of delight, and all his energies are taken captive on behalf of the enemy of good! In other words, he loses his authority (his palace), his peace (his fortresses), his delight (in the house of Eden) and all his energies!

1.3.11.en: This is what the Lord meant by the chastisement of Damascus… that man may realize what complete deprivation and total destruction he has reached, and so flee to God alone, who restores to him what he lost, doubled, on a supreme heavenly level!

1.4.0.en: 6 Thus saith the LORD; “For three transgressions of Gaza, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they carried away captive the whole captivity, to deliver them up to Edom: 7 But I will send a fire on the wall of Gaza, which shall devour the palaces thereof: 8 And I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, and him that holdeth the sceptre from Ashkelon, and I will turn mine hand against Ekron: and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish, saith the Lord GOD.”

1.4.1.en: Gaza was the capital of Philistia at that time, and the sin of Philistia at that time was their exploitation of the sons of Judah who fled to them from before Sennacherib king of Assyria, seizing them and selling them as slaves to the sons of Edom, their bitterest enemies. They wanted to wipe out the name of Israel at that time, as the psalmist says: “They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance” (Ps 83:4). Therefore the fire that turned back upon them was to devour the palaces of the principal cities: Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon and Ekron.

1.4.2.en: St. Augustine sees that the word Philistines means “those who fall from drunkenness,” and so it points to the souls that become drunk with the love of the world and its luxury. St. Jerome interprets this name as “death by a poisonous draught,” and in his view they represent those who drink the cup of Satan’s seduction as a poison for the soul that destroys it, so that they fall quickly.

1.5.0.en: 9 Thus saith the LORD; “For three transgressions of Tyrus, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they delivered up the whole captivity to Edom, and remembered not the brotherly covenant: 10 But I will send a fire on the wall of Tyrus, which shall devour the palaces thereof.”

1.5.1.en: Phoenicia, whose capital was Tyre, took pride in its navy and its enormous trade on a strong international level.

1.5.2.en: Tyre forgot the treaty of brotherhood between their king Hiram and King Solomon (1 Kgs 5:1-12; 9:10-14), and sold the Israelites who fled to them as slaves to their enemy Edom. Therefore God allowed the fires to burn their palaces for the betrayal of the brotherly covenant, and this was fulfilled literally when Nebuchadnezzar besieged it and captured it in the sixth century B.C.

1.5.3.en: St. Jerome and St. Augustine see that the word “Tyre” means distress or trial. Therefore what is said about Tyre, especially in the Book of Ezekiel (chapter 28), points to Satan, who pushes people into satanic trials and temptations.

1.6.0.en: 11 Thus saith the LORD; “For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because he did pursue his brother with the sword, and did cast off all pity, and his anger did tear perpetually, and he kept his wrath for ever: 12 But I will send a fire upon Teman, which shall devour the palaces of Bozrah.”

1.6.1.en: Edom is Esau, the brother of Jacob, and the sons of Edom took a hostile position toward the sons of Israel (Jacob) when they passed through the wilderness, for they did not allow them to pass (Num 20:13-21), and they always stood in a position of gloating over the sons of Israel, and sometimes even carried out destructive attacks.

1.6.2.en: The word “Edom” is taken from “Adam,” and means “a bloody man,” or “earthly,” and points to the love of shedding blood for the sake of earthly things.

1.6.3.en: If Edom was inflamed with the fire of evil and the love of shedding blood, the fire turns back upon him to burn the palaces of the most important of his regions, Teman (Teman is a tribe named after the firstborn of Eliphaz the son of Esau), and the regions it inhabits (Gen 36:11, 15, 42). The region lies in the north of Edom (Ezek 35:13), and its inhabitants were known for your wisdom (Jer 49:7).

1.6.4.en: As for Bozrah, whose palaces are burned, it is a city in the land of Edom (Isa 34:6; 63:1). The word “Bozrah” means in Hebrew “fortress” or “sheepfold,” and it was utterly ruined as the prophet Jeremiah prophesied concerning it (Jer 49:13)… If Bozrah, with its potentials, represents the fortress of Teman in Edom, then evil burns its goods and destroys its potentials and makes it a ruin.

1.7.s.en: 6. The chastisement of the children of Ammon:

1.7.0.en: 13 Thus saith the LORD; “For three transgressions of the children of Ammon, and for four, I will not turn away the punishment thereof; because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border: 14 But I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall devour the palaces thereof, with shouting in the day of battle, with a tempest in the day of the whirlwind: 15 And their king shall go into captivity, he and his princes together, saith the LORD.”

1.7.1.en: In our study of the Book of Ezekiel we saw that the children of Ammon, the descendants of Ben-ammi the son of Lot (Gen 19:38), were hard of heart and offered their children as sacrifices to the god Milcom (1 Kgs 11:5-33). They were in constant war with the sons of Israel.

1.7.2.en: The sons of Ammon represent cruelty based on greed: “because they have ripped up the women with child of Gilead, that they might enlarge their border” [13]. Thus greed corrupts the humanity of man and his natural tenderness, for the sake of an earthly gain the womb of pregnant women is ripped open, killing them and tormenting them and making them lose their unborn children! A hideous picture of the heart that the earth turns into a predatory beast, having no mercy on the weak women or on the unborn children, who have no guilt and no strength!

1.7.3.en: As for its natural fruit, the fires devour the walls of its capital Rabbah (Amman) and burn its palaces, and it turns into a region of battle and tempests, and its king and his great men are taken captive. If “Rabbah” means “great,” then the man who is cruel to others and shatters them for his own earthly benefit, to be great over all and richer than all, loses his walls and his palaces are burned and his inner life turns into a field of bitter battle, and he loses his true peace, and his mind and heart and all his energies are taken captive to what belongs to the enemy. He comes to a state of complete loss of everything! For while he thinks that he is acquiring by his strength and power, behold, he enters into a severe emptiness, and a loss even of his life and his peace and his potentials!
